summary: Replaced mymatasan's single admin/non-admin bool authorization with a three-role permission matrix (viewer, operator, admin), fixing two real security gaps: previously there was no read authorization at all (any signed-in user could read every camera, recording, and alert snapshot), and 'may watch cameras but may not delete recordings' was not expressible, the property that makes an NVR evidentiary rather than a camera viewer. mymatasan now reuses the shared accessrbac role/permission data model (domain/shared/services/access_rbac.go, whose path matcher was upgraded to segment-wise matching with a single-segment '*' wildcard, specificity-based row selection instead of raw string length, and a refusal to store a root-path '/' grant-everything row) with its own middleware (apis.NewRequireRolePermission), since mymatasan has no JWT to satisfy the shared session middleware. The authorization catalog is Go data (apps/mymatasan/services/rbac.go's Policy()): viewer watches live and sees that an alert fired with no footage access; operator adds reviewing/downloading recorded footage, acknowledging alerts, PTZ, and talk-back but can never delete or purge anything or reconfigure the system; admin (the shared superadmin builtin) bypasses the matrix. The parent-to-node control tunnel (apis/control_dispatch.go) now carries a role NAME rather than an admin/viewer bool, and the node resolves it against its own roles and evaluates its own matrix rather than trusting the parent's assertion, closing a projection gap where a fine-grained fleet role used to collapse into a raw admin/not-admin flag at every node.
compatibility: No config change and no manual step required. On first boot after upgrade, every local user without a role yet is auto-assigned one derived from their legacy isAdmin flag: existing admins become admin, and every other existing user becomes operator (deliberately not the stricter viewer, since operator preserves everything a non-admin could already do -- review footage and acknowledge alerts -- with no loss of access; they additionally gain PTZ and talk-back, a small documented widening). The legacy isAdmin field still works end-to-end: it is retained on the entity as a mirror written from the resolved role (never read for authorization), and the user create/update API still accepts a bare isAdmin bool from clients that predate roles (falls back to superadmin/viewer when roleId is omitted). The control-channel wire vocabulary widened from {admin, viewer} to {admin, operator, viewer}; an older control plane sending only 'admin'/'viewer' keeps working unchanged (admin is kept as a wire alias for the superadmin role). Existing shared accessrbac permission rows elsewhere in the suite (myseliasan, myidsan) are unaffected: every stored row is wildcard-free, so the new segment-wise path matching and specificity ranking are semantically identical to the old prefix matching for them. Known follow-ups (not done here): myseliasan's NodeAccessGrant still has only CanRead/CanWrite bools and needs a third level to map a fleet operator onto a node's new operator role; the frontend has no role picker yet, so assigning operator today requires calling the API directly with a roleId.
